content.title: Is Target open on Easter
content.text: Donald Trump was dealt some bad news in his ongoing feud with Pope Leo XIV, as MS Now interrupted regular programming to share a setback for him regarding his policies, which don’t reflect the Christian values he claimed to uphold. The president, 79, has been under fire when it comes to religion since Easter Sunday, one of the holiest days of the Christian faith, when he opted out of attending any church services and posted threats against Iran. In the time since, he has also taken aim at the Pope, as well as posted and deleted a social media post that depicted him as Jesus Christ healing a man who looked very similar to The Daily Show’s Jon Stewart. • Trump's 'lunatic' answer when asked what his favorite Bible verse is causes outrage • Fox News viewers turn on Karoline Leavitt as they fume over tax refund claims On the Wednesday, April 15 episode of The Briefing with Jen Psaki, the former Biden Press Secretary, 47, discussed the story with Andy Beshear, the Democratic governor of Kentucky. While on the show, Beshear delivered a scathing rebuke of Trump’s alleged religious beliefs, pointing out several ways he didn’t follow the teachings of the church. “Jesus served the lost, the lonely, and the left behind,” he said. “He tried to lift people up while they were down, and Donald Trump just tries to kick them while they’re there. Jesus ministered to the poor and to the migrants. Yet that is who this administration goes after.” “...everything about Christianity teaches us not to judge, teaches us to accept and teaches us to love one another,” he continued. “I was sure that our President had not read the bible before, but during the funeral of Charlie Kirk, Erika Kirk comes out and actually lives out the golden rule. I will give her credit. In the toughest moment, she said that she’s going to love her enemies.” “And Donald Trump walks out and says, ‘No, no, I hate them,'" he added. After the clip surfaced on social media, the bad news continued to roll in for the president, as many viewers agreed with the assessment. “It’s as if Jesus said it MAGA immediately thought do the opposite because that’s what Jesus would want them to do and fight in their own righteous holy war,” one person wrote on X (formerly Twitter). “Republicans love the optics of being religious the teachings not so much. Look at what they do, not what they say,” a second said. “Trump doesn’t realize his obnoxious sacreligious attacks on the Catholic Church has created a rebirth of faith and increased displeasure with your leadership,” a third added. “In MAGA heaven, Saint Pete’s only job is to collect a cover charge,” a fourth snarked. The commentary comes as supporters have slammed the feud Trump has seemingly picked with the pope, after he called the president’s threats toward Iran “unacceptable,” and Trump responded by calling him “weak” and captive to the “radical left.” Visitors to the Vatican took aim at Trump as they visited the holy site. “It’s just ridiculous, because of the Pope is not speaking about peace, and is not taking care about every people in the world, he’s not the Pope,” Joerg Soler, who was visiting from Switzerland, said. American tourist Paul Sarauskas also called the president’s comments “absurd,” saying, “I think he needs to keep his nose out of religion. He’s telling the Pope what to do. He’s telling the Pope how to do his job.” “Where the Pope just wants to do good things, right? He wants to talk about peace, about helping other people, whereas the current administration is doing something completely opposite. They’re just tearing people apart. They’re talking about division and war and hate.” It comes after a disturbing detail in Trump's AI Jesus photo was spotted by disgusted viewers.
